# DataWeave changes

Follow the project's existing DataWeave conventions first. Check the executing runtime and the app's `minMuleVersion`, which sets the language level (Mule 4.4 gives 2.4, through 4.9 giving 2.9); `%dw 2.0` alone does not identify the engine version. See [versioning behavior](https://docs.mulesoft.com/dataweave/2.9/dataweave-versioning-behavior). State the input and output MIME types and shape, and define behavior for absent, null, empty, malformed and unexpected-type values before writing the mapping. Items marked (documented) are stated in MuleSoft documentation for 2.9 (Mule 4.9); items marked (CLI) were observed with the DataWeave CLI (runtime 2.12.2, language levels 2.4–2.9), so confirm them on the project's runtime when they decide the outcome.

Four reference files hold situational detail. Read the one that applies before writing that code. If you cannot open files yourself, say which one the change needs and ask for it to be attached.

- [Correctness details](../skills/team-mule-guardrails/references/dataweave-correctness.md): before moving a script or changing its header or another Transform output; using `default` or validating malformed input; parsing or formatting numbers or dates; handling null collections, object equality, repeated keys or XML selectors, object keys, joins or sorting; or writing overloaded functions or shared modules.
- [Operator and function behavior](../skills/team-mule-guardrails/references/dataweave-operators.md): before using `-` or `--`, range selectors, `take`/`drop`/`slice`, `update`, `mask` or the `dw::util::Tree` helpers, or `isBlank`/`trim`/`upper`, or writing a recursive function.
- [Output formats](../skills/team-mule-guardrails/references/dataweave-output-formats.md): before changing an `output` directive or its writer properties, including JSON options such as `skipNullOn`, or writing CSV or XML.
- [Performance and large payloads](../skills/team-mule-guardrails/references/dataweave-performance.md): before optimizing a script, reading large inputs, changing lookups or streaming, or using `deferred`, `log()` or `output application/dw`.

## Check these first

Each rule here corrected a mistake that recurred when assistants were tested on DataWeave tasks.

- Chains and precedence: when another call follows a lambda, wrap the lambda in parentheses, `items filter ((i) -> i.price < 100) map ((i) -> i.sku)`. Without them the lambda body runs to the end of the expression, so the next call receives a Boolean and the script fails (CLI). Comparisons bind more tightly than `and` and `or`, which bind more tightly than `matches`, `map` and `filter`, so `q is String and q matches /\d+/` fails; write `(q is String) and (q matches /\d+/)` (documented). `!` negates only the next operand while `not` negates everything after it, so write `!(q matches /\d+/)` (documented). `i mod 3 == 0` passes `3 == 0` to `mod`; write `(i mod 3) == 0` (CLI). In `match`, put a type test inside the condition, `case s if ((s is String) and (s matches /\d+/)) ->`, as MuleSoft's example does; `case s is String if (...)` does not parse (CLI). See [pattern matching](https://docs.mulesoft.com/dataweave/2.9/dataweave-pattern-matching), [precedence](https://docs.mulesoft.com/dataweave/2.9/dataweave-flow-control-precedence) and [operators](https://docs.mulesoft.com/dataweave/2.9/dw-operators).
- Imports: functions in `dw::Core`, such as `isBlank`, `sizeOf` and `joinBy`, are imported automatically, and functions in any other module need an import, for example `import fail from dw::Runtime`, `import take from dw::core::Arrays` or `import mergeWith from dw::core::Objects` (documented). Importing a Core function from another module fails: `import isBlank from dw::core::Strings` does not resolve (CLI). DataWeave has no `indexBy` (CLI). Use only functions documented for the project's language level; `take`, for example, was introduced in 2.2.0. See [functions and modules](https://docs.mulesoft.com/dataweave/2.9/dw-functions).
- Variables: declare `var`, `fun`, `type` and `import` in the header, before `---`; a `var` written after `---` does not compile (CLI). For a local variable in the body, use a `do` scope, `do { var items = payload.items default [] --- items map $.sku }` (documented). See [variables](https://docs.mulesoft.com/dataweave/2.9/dataweave-variables).
- Joining text: `++` joins two Strings (documented), and `"a" ++ null` fails at runtime (CLI). A value typed `String | Null` still fails to compile in `++` after an `isEmpty` check, though a `== null` check works (CLI). Default each optional part first, `(p.middleName default "")`, or collect the parts in an array, drop the empty ones and use `joinBy`. See [++](https://docs.mulesoft.com/dataweave/2.9/dw-core-functions-plusplus).
- Lookups: build a lookup once with `groupBy` and index it with a String key, `byId[(o.customerId as String)]`. Indexing an object with a Number selects by position: after `groupBy $.id`, `grouped[201]` returned `null` and `grouped[1]` returned the second group, not key `"1"` (CLI). A lookup such as `filter(...)[0]` or `grouped[k][0]` returns `null` when nothing matches; decide and test what the output should be.
- Merging objects: `++` on objects with a shared key keeps both keys: JSON output repeats the key and `.key` returns the first value (CLI). Use `mergeWith` from `dw::core::Objects` (right-hand values win) or remove the key first. JSON input with duplicate keys also keeps both.
- Conditional array items and object fields need parentheses: `[(x) if cond]`, `{(key: v) if cond}`; without them the script does not compile (CLI). Wrap a compound condition in one pair, `{(key: v) if ((a) and (b))}`; `if (a) and (b)` does not compile (CLI). When the contract says to leave a field out, omit it rather than writing `null`. Use `flatMap` instead of `flatten` around a `map`.
- Time zones: a time-zone literal must be an offset such as `|-06:00|` (documented); `|America/Chicago|` does not parse (CLI). Coerce a zone ID from a string and attach it to a local date-time, `(local as LocalDateTime) ++ ("America/Chicago" as TimeZone)`, then shift with `>> "UTC"`. See [date and time types](https://docs.mulesoft.com/dataweave/2.9/dataweave-types#dw_type_dates).
- XML escaping: in an attribute such as `expression="#[...]"`, the expression is XML attribute text: write `<` as `&lt;` and `&` as `&amp;`, and inside a double-quoted attribute use single-quoted DataWeave strings (CLI) or `&quot;`. Inside `<![CDATA[ ... ]]>`, write `<`, `&` and quotes unescaped, since entities such as `&lt;` are not decoded there, and never write `]]>`, which ends the section: put a space in `arr[idx[0]] > 5`. Keep the file's escaping style; after any edit the file must still be well-formed XML. See [XML character data](https://www.w3.org/TR/xml/#syntax).
- Rounding: formatting rounds half up (`2.345` gives `"2.35"`) and `round(-2.5)` is `-3` (CLI). For banker's rounding or another mode, pass `roundMode`: `x as String {format: "0.00", roundMode: "HALF_EVEN"}` (CLI). See [toString](https://docs.mulesoft.com/dataweave/2.9/dw-coercions-functions-tostring).
- Splitting: `splitBy` drops trailing empty fields (`"a,b,"` gives `["a","b"]`) and returns `[""]` for `""` (CLI). Use the CSV reader, or restore the trailing fields explicitly, when empty fields matter.

## Testing

Scripts in a flow use Mule's predefined variables (`payload`, `attributes`, `vars`, `error` and others) and Mule functions such as `p()`, which the standalone DataWeave CLI does not have (CLI). To test a script outside Mule, copy it to a scratch file outside the project and supply those values as inputs, or cover the flow with MUnit. See [predefined variables](https://docs.mulesoft.com/dataweave/2.9/dataweave-variables-context). Check realistic samples and adversarial boundaries: zero and false, absent and null, empty arrays and strings, malformed numbers and dates, and Unicode when relevant; successful JSON parsing alone does not test DataWeave. If the project already uses the DataWeave testing framework (`src/test/dw`), add tests there; do not add that dependency without approval.
